summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 117% YoY to INR2,408 crore and PAT more than tripled to about INR62.6 crore, driven mainly by LPG volumes.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue (about INR2,408 crore), EBITDA (about INR147 crore) and PAT (about INR62.6 crore) for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with basic EPS of INR1.86. Management attributed the top-line jump largely to higher LPG prices during supply disruption from West Asia, while saying volumes also rose sharply (about doubled YoY) and that a portion of the growth came from new bulk and institutional customers on short- to medium-term contracts. Auto LPG volumes slowed temporarily on higher prices and have since recovered per management. Most company-specific numbers (segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes, Type 4 cylinder margins) were deferred to follow-up emails.

financial_highlights.change: +117% YoY (from INR1,112 crore); +98% QoQ (from INR1,216 crore)

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR62.6 crore (management also cited exceeding INR66 crore in one remark)
financial_highlights.change: More than tripled YoY (from INR20.5 crore); +82% QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: PAT margin (analyst-cited, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.change: Management said margins are 'intact' and that the drop is due to higher LPG prices

segments.name: Packed LPG (GoGas)
segments.commentary: Packed LPG sales of about 18,000-20,000 MT per month; management said it is more commercial than domestic and price-competitive on commercial. Packed LPG and Auto LPG were named as the highest-EBITDA-margin segments, but no margin figures were given.

segments.name: Bulk LPG / industrial
segments.commentary: About 300 industrial customers served; new accounts added in FMCG, food processing, glass and ceramics. Management said a meaningful part of Q1 was volume-led from new bulk and institutional customers.

segments.name: Auto LPG (ALDS)
segments.commentary: 315+ dispensing stations, all operational. Demand slowed temporarily in the quarter on higher LPG prices, and management said volumes have since recovered. Payback on a new station is said to be under 18 months.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: 50+ CNG stations completed, with a further 50 targeted in Bengaluru. Average station volume was said to be about 6,000-6,200 kg per day, and total volume about 3 lakh kg per day.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 10-15% QoQ growth in revenue, PAT and EBITDA in coming quarters; it did not give a multi-year revenue number.
Auto LPG network target: 500 stations, with about 75 added in FY27 and about 100 in FY28, then a further evaluation toward 500.
CNG target to increase from 50 to 100 stations; talks with other CGD players for Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore, not finalised.
Management expects margins to rise as volumes grow and once prices normalise; no bps or percentage target was given.
Backward integration is under evaluation, including small coastal storage terminals (not finalised) and a 100% Dubai subsidiary for LPG import ease.
Type 4 high-pressure cylinder unit at Butibori (Nagpur): capex complete and machinery installed; production expected in 1-2 months, subject to order book. Margin not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Type 4 high-pressure cylinder plant (Butibori): capex complete and machinery installed; start awaits order book, with production expected in 1-2 months. Target customers are CGD players, car fleet owners and OEMs.
CNG: 50+ stations operational; 50 more planned in Bengaluru.
Auto LPG: 315+ stations; target 500 (75 in FY27, 100 in FY28).

Fleet and infrastructure as stated: ships on time charter, 68+ bottling/blending plants, 478+ LPG road tankers, 225+ HCVs/LCVs, 82 CNG road vehicles, 15 cylinder plants and 3 high-pressure cylinder plants.
Total capacity was cited by an analyst as 608 TMT or 685 TMT; management did not confirm or answer on utilisation.
demand_pricing: India LPG market about 35.04 MMT, projected at about 40-42 MMT by FY2030; OMCs hold about 94% of sales and private marketers about 6%, with CPIL holding about 33% of the private segment (management claim).
During the West Asia disruption, the company diversified sourcing to North America, Africa and the Middle East, and said several marquee customers moved to longer-term contracts.
Management said Q1 revenue growth was mainly price-driven, but also volume-driven (volumes about doubled YoY per management).
Management said it is price-competitive against PSUs in industrial, HoReCa and commercial segments.
Gin Kar Lo, Gin Kar Do scheme (pay-for-actual-consumption cylinder weighing) introduced; direct financial impact not a stated objective.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Type 4 cylinder plant operational, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is complete and machinery is installed at Butibori. Production is expected within 1-2 months, but the start depends on receiving the order book. Management declined to give margin numbers until the first deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: Which cities are in CNG network talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Mumbai, Hyderabad and Indore were named, but none is finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue, EBITDA and PAT will grow QoQ, though revenue will move with LPG prices. It later quantified 10-15% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the PAT margin trending and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are intact and rising, and that the lower percentage reflects higher LPG prices. It gave no quantified margin target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth came from the West Asia disruption, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company had inventory when PSUs faced constraints, and that new customers signed longer-term agreements. Management said volumes are sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation priority (organic, M&A, debt, dividends)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of new stations, JVs and acquiring infrastructure, plus bottling expansion and backward integration. No allocation split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging of LPG import currency exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments are made on time and spot contracts are used, so no hedge is currently required; it would hedge in future if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BW exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BW, a strategic investor from 2023-24, exited in the secondary market to focus on its shipping business, with no impact on the company.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Income Tax search?
qa_highlights.answer: The search began 7 October 2025 and closed within 7 days. Assessment is open, no final demand has been received, and management does not expect a large payable.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of revenue by segment, FY26 capex, and LPG import data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred these to follow-up emails and gave no figures on the call.

risks_watch: Revenue is price-driven: management said revenue will fluctuate with LPG prices, so the QoQ 10-15% guidance is not tied to a price assumption and may not hold if prices fall.
Margin trajectory is unquantified: management said PAT margins are intact and will rise, but gave no bps target, and the analyst-cited PAT margin (about 2.5-3%) was not confirmed.
Type 4 cylinder plant at Butibori: start depends on receiving an order book; no customer contracts were confirmed and no margin was disclosed.
Auto LPG volumes slowed on higher prices in Q1 and management says they have since recovered; watch monthly volume data and the 75 station additions in FY27.
Open items: segment revenue split, FY26 capex, LPG import volumes and per-ton EBITDA were deferred to email; Income Tax assessment remains open with no final demand.
Sustainability of West Asia-linked volume gains: management said several customers moved to longer-term contracts, but terms and volumes were not disclosed.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has taken our momentum significantly further, with revenue crossing INR2,408 crores and PAT exceeding INR66 crores.
But actually, the profit margins are not declined. They are intact and they are increasing day-by-day.
So, in terms of percentage, we will increase our revenue and PAT by, say, quarter -on-quarter 10% to 15%.

So, basically, once the plant get operationalized and we will start delivering our first round of cylinders, we will evaluate and we will revert you, because right now if I commit any numbers, it will be a little bit challenging.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on growth and sustainability of volumes, but cautious and evasive on margins, segment economics and FY26 capex, deferring several figures to follow-up emails. Its answers on profitability repeatedly shifted to absolute PAT and the "intact" margin argument rather than quantified percentages.
